articles.headline: MLB Hot Stove tracker: Live updates on latest news, rumors, signings and trades in 2026 free agency
keyFacts: An MLB lockout is set to begin on December 1, halting all player transactions until a new collective bargaining agreement is reached.
The New York Mets agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with top free-agent pitcher Tarik Skubal.
Multiple teams have completed player signings and trades, including the Cubs adding outfielder Teruki Sato on a six-year, $120 million contract.
body: The heart of the MLB offseason is typically the first two weeks of December, but this isn't a typical offseason.

A lockout is set to take effect at the end of the day on Dec. 1, ending all transactions until the owners and players agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. As we saw five years ago, that will likely take some time.

2021 offers an indication of how offseason transactions could play out: there was a flurry of activity leading up to start of the lockout, but plenty of significant moves had to wait until after the lockout was lifted more than three months later.
If reports are any indication, though, No. 1 free agent Tarik Skubal has a strong chance to sign before the lockout begins, raising the level of intrigue around free agency.
The Sporting News is tracking the latest MLB rumors, signings and trades before the lockout begins. Follow along below with the latest news.
MLB Hot Stove 2026: Latest news, rumors on signings and trades
Diamondbacks sign Japanese pitcher Kona Takahashi
The Diamondbacks acquired RHP Kona Takahashi on a one-year free-agent contract. The 6-foot-2 pitcher posted a 9-6 record, a 2.54 ERA and 114 strikeouts in the NPB last season.
Jazz Chisholm finalizing deal with Blue Jays

The Toronto Blue Jays are signing former Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm, according to Jon Heyman. Chisholm posted a .711 OPS with New York last season and hit .231 with just 19 HRs in 532 plate appearances. According to ESPN's Jeff Passan, the contract is a one-year deal for $12.5 million with a player option for a second year at $16 million.
Diamondbacks land former No. 1 pick Henry Davis

The Diamondbacks acquired catcher Henry Davis from the Pirates in exchange for utilityman Tim Tawa. Davis, 27, was selected No. 1 overall in the 2021 MLB Draft. He tallied 10 home runs and 38 RBIs with a .585 OPS in 298 plate appearances in 2026.
Nationals add A.J. Puk to bullpen
The Nationals have agreed to a one-year, $5 million deal with left-handed reliever A.J. Puk.

The Twins are signing former Diamondbacks reliever Kevin Ginkel to a two-year, $18 million contract. Ginkel played a key role in Arizona's run to the 2023 World Series but had a rockier stretch between 2025 and 2025.
Rockies add Patrick Sandoval to overhauled rotation

The Rockies have agreed to a three-year, $42 million deal with starter Patrick Sandoval, making him the fourth starting pitcher to join Colorado within the last week. Sandoval had a 5.12 ERA but much more promising 3.77 FIP across 13 starts with the Red Sox in 2026 after missing all of 2025 with Tommy John Surgery.

The Orioles are bringing back OF Luis Robert on a one-year, $12 million deal. Baltimore claimed Robert off waivers from the Mets late in the season to no avail, as the team quickly faded from postseason contention, but the Orioles are giving it another shot and reportedly plan to utilize him as their everyday centerfielder.
Rockies add David Peterson to rotation

The Rockies have agreed to a two-year, $32 million deal with starter David Peterson. Peterson split 2026 with the Mets and Cubs, struggling in New York but posting a 3.70 ERA across 80.1 innings in Chicago to rebuild his value.

The Tigers have agreed to a one-year, $25 million deal with veteran starter Kevin Gausman. A workhorse with at least 31 starts in each of the last six seasons, Gausman regressed with the Blue Jays and Cubs in 2026 but had better underlying numbers with a 3.74 FIP.

The Guardians are re-signing starter Foster Griffin to a three-year, $48 million deal. Griffin was a terrific story with the Nationals in 2026, and his rocky 5.19 ERA in nine starts with the Guardians comes with the caveat that his underlying numbers were actually better in Cleveland than they were in Washington.

After winning the World Series with the Brewers, veteran catcher Gary Sanchez has agreed to a one-year, $6.5 million deal with the Marlins. Sanchez figures to serve as the backup to young catcher Joe Mack.

As the Padres face the likely exit of Adrian Morejon, they have agreed to a three-year, $21 million deal with former Cardinals and Brewers reliever JoJo Romero. Romero, who split 2026 between the two NL Central clubs, has a 2.91 ERA over the last three seasons.

The Brewers are re-signing reliever Antonio Senzatela to a one-year, $4.75 million contract. Milwaukee acquired Senzatela from the Rockies at the August deadline, and the former starter had a rocky 5.14 ERA across 23 appearances with the Brewers before a better postseason.

Alec Bohm's time with the Phillies is over, and he's headed to Kansas City. The Royals are signing the third baseman on a two-year, $20 million deal. The move comes on the heels of the Maikel Garcia trade to the Mariners, opening a spot in KC's corner infield.
Reds bring back Tyler Stephenson on 3-year deal

The Reds are re-signing catcher Tyler Stephenson to a three-year, $30 million contract with an opt-out after 2028. Cincinnati surprised many by not trading Stephenson at the deadline in August, but the decision makes more sense with a deal to bring back the team's serviceable starting catcher.

The White Sox and OF Tyrone Taylor have agreed to a two-year, $17 million deal. Taylor was excellent against left-handed pitching with the Mets and Cubs in 2026 and plays solid defense, so he will at the very least be a valuable platoon player as he heads to the South Side.
Blue Jays bringing in Japanese free agent Kaima Taira on 5-year deal

One year after the Blue Jays signed Japanese free agent Kazuma Okamoto, Toronto is bringing in another player from overseas, inking Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million contract with an opt-out after the third season. The deal also includes a $5 million signing bonus for the right-handed pitcher. The Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and pivot to the 27-year-old to pair with Dylan Cease in the rotation. Taira switched between the rotation and bullpen of the Seibu Lions over the last few season, but posted a 1.36 ERA as a full-time starter in 2026.
Tigers add Ha-Seong Kim to infield

The Tigers are adding infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million deal. Kim struggled mightily offensively with the Braves in 2026, batting a career-low .116 with a .216 OBP. Detroit is hoping that it's an anomaly and Kim can provide some depth in the infield.
Orioles make massive move to sign Freddy Peralta

Freddy Peralta is cashing in. After reviving his season with the Rays in the back half of this year, the Orioles are bringing in the right-hander to headline their rotation. Peralta struggled to start 2026 with the Mets, but a trade to Tampa Bay worked wonders for him. He went 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts and was stellar in the Rays' run to the World Series, recording an astonishing 2.95 ERA in five appearances.

The Guardians are adding to their pitching staff, signing lefty Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million deal. The 29-year-old split his time between the Royals and Dodgers last year, traded to L.A. at the deadline. He was limited to just nine starts and 14 appearances, posting a 3.76 ERA.
Cubs land Japanese free agent Teruki Sato

The top Japanese free agent of the 2026 offseason is heading to Chicago as the Cubs have reportedly agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract for the outfielder. The 27-year-old won the Triple Crown for the Hanshin Tigers this year and is a two-time Central League MVP. Sato is expected to play corner outfield, likely replacing free agent Seiya Suzuki.

The Cubs are bolstering their rotation, signing lefty Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract. Rogers broke out with the Orioles in 2025, posting a 1.81 ERA and 9-3 record, but he regressed back to the norm this past year, going 10-11 with a 4.03 ERA. Chicago is hoping he finds his 2025 form again in the Windy City.

New York adds the 37-year-old Suter on a one-year deal worth $4 million as the Yankees aim to reshape their bullpen. Suter has been both a starter and reliever in his career, and he will start out the season in the Yankees' bullpen.
Teruaki Sato could sign before Thanksgiving

The Japanese star needs to sign before the pending lockout next week, and it seems like he is on track to sign somewhere this week. The Phillies, Blue Jays, Yankees and Mets are all teams that have been linked to the slugger.

The veteran Goldshmidt isn't the star he used to be, but he can still defend at first base and hit lefties after serving as a platoon player with the Yankees. He will likely form a platoon with Jared Young at first base for the Mets next season.
Tarik Skubal agrees to deal with Mets

The Mets have agreed to a nine-year, $450 million deal with Skubal, Jon Heyman and Jeff Passan report. Skubal's free agency ends more than a week before the lockout as the Mets make him by far the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history in terms of both total value and average annual value.
Tigers add former Rookie of the Year Luis Gil

The Tigers have agreed to a one-year, $2.3 million deal with non-tendered former Yankees starter Luis Gil. Gil was the AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 but has battled injuries and control issues over the last two seasons while also seeing his strikeout rate plummet.
Jarren Duran drawing interest from several teams

Red Sox OF Jarren Duran remains a trade candidate despite being tendered a contract and is drawing interest from the Padres, Phillies and Mariners, MassLive reports. The Cubs were previously reported as another suitor for Duran.

Fresh off a resurgent season with the Padres, free-agent Ty France is reportedly seeking a three-year deal. The Athletic reports France is looking for an average annual salary between Jake Bauers' $14.5 million and Jorge Polanco's $20 million from last winter.
Mets offered Skubal nine-year deal worth almost $400 million

The Mets appear to be the most aggressive suitor for Skubal, with an initial offer that would allow Skubal to break multiple pitching contract records. Skubal also met with the Blue Jays, Dodgers and Padres thus far.
Cubs claim catcher Joey Bart off waivers

The former No. 2 overall pick heads to the Cubs after he played for multiple teams in 2026. He should be a depth catcher option and could ultimately replace Carson Kelly, who is a free agent this offseason.
Jonathan Loaisiga goes back to Yankees

It's a two-year deal for Loaisiga, with a club option for the 2029 season, as the reliever returns to New York after a year with the Diamondbacks. Loaisiga battled injuries in his first stint with the Yankees, but he was great for Arizona in 2026 as he had a bounce-back season, and now he cashes in.

The Cubs have "extensively" scouted Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, The Athletic's Patrick Mooney reports. Sato is currently posted for MLB teams and is the consensus top international free agent on the market.
Yankees involved in third base market
The Yankees checked in on Maikel Garcia before he was traded, Jon Morosi reports, and are in the market for a third base upgrade.
Tarik Skubal still likely to sign before lockout
Skubal has met with all four teams publicly reported as suitors and is "likely" to sign before the lockout takes effect at the end of Dec. 1, Jon Heyman reports.
Padres 'could be the favorites' for Seiya Suzuki

The Padres met with free-agent OF Seiya Suzuki on Monday and "could be the favorites" to sign him, according to Jeff Passan. Suzuki is one of this offseason's top available bats after a strong five seasons with the Cubs.
Twins ink Sonny Gray to 2-year deal

Sonny Gray is returning to Minnesota for a second stint, as the Twins announced he has signed a two-year deal with the team. The deal is worth $55 million, according to Jon Heyman. Gray received down-ballot Cy Young votes in his lone season with the Red Sox, posting a 2.72 ERA across 29 starts.
Red Sox acquire Nick Fortes from Rays

The Red Sox are acquiring catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays for 17-year-old pitching prospect Angel Roa. Fortes, 30, is a defense-first catcher who hit .258 with 6 home runs across 109 games in Tampa Bay last season.
Mariners acquire Maikel Garcia in 6-player deal
The Mariners have acquired 3B Maikel Garcia, RP James McArthur and minor-league RP L.P. Langevin from the Royals, in exchange for SP Bryce Miller, SP Logan Evans and RP Jose Ferrer.

Garcia broke out as an All-Star in 2025 with an .800 OPS and Gold Glove defense. While he regressed offensively, Garcia offers a high floor with his excellent defense and is under team control through 2030.
Miller, under contract through 2029, gives the Royals an instant rotation option as Kansas City adds much-needed pitching across the board.
David Bednar, Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer

After four players took themselves off the market last winter by accepting qualifying offers, two did so on Tuesday: Yankees closer David Bednar and Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers will both return on the one-year, $23.15 million deal. Bednar notched 35 saves in a strong season as New York's closer in 2026, while Jeffers was limited to just 92 games but posted an .814 OPS and 2.8 WAR in that span.
White Sox sign SP Dustin May

The White Sox are signing May to a three-year contract worth "just north" of $50 million, per Murray. The right-hander won another World Series with the Brewers this past season, but has been up-and-down since a 2.63 ERA season with the Dodgers in 2023. May will bring some strikeout stuff to Chicago's rotation.
Brewers acquire reliever Ryan Walker from Giants

The Giants have traded reliever Ryan Walker to the Brewers for minor-league pitchers Gavin Perry and Blake Holub. A standout with a 1.91 ERA in 2024, Walker regressed sharply in 2024 and fell out of the big-league bullpen with a 7.16 ERA in 2026; he's under team control through 2029.
Orioles, Diamondbacks discussing Ketel Marte swap

The Orioles are reportedly interested in landing Marte from the Diamondbacks via trade. The three-time All-Star has twice finished inside the top-four in NL MVP voting. Marte, 33, posted a .748 OPS and 107 OPS+ in 562 at-bats last year.
Red Sox, Jake Bauers agree terms to four-year deal

Boston locked up Bauers, the NLCS MVP, on a four-year, $58 million deal. Bauers, 31, enjoyed the best season of his big-league career in 2026, posting an .874 OPS and 140 OPS+ while slugging 26 home runs in 144 games.

The Braves add the reliever on a three-year, $35 million deal to help upgrade the bullpen and potentially replace Raisel Iglesias. Phillips broke out with the Dodgers since joining Los Angeles in 2021, totaling a 2.36 ERA in 232 games with the team.
Phillies expressing interest in Teruaki Sato, Seiya Suzuki, Randy Arozarena

Philadelphia is looking to add an outfielder and has looked at three of the top bats in Sato, Suzuki and Arozarena; the Phillies are 'intrigued' by Sato, who has been posted to MLB teams after winning a triple-crown in Japan's Central League.
The Yankees have been monitoring third baseman Alec Bohm on the free-agent market, with the potential to bring him in to hit primarily vs. left-handed pitchers.
Braves shut down ideas of trading Ronald Acuna Jr.
After some rumors that the Braves could look into trading star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr., Alex Anthopoulos shut them down, saying: "We are not trading Ronald Acuna Jr. Put it in bold."
Anthopoulos added that Atlanta has had " zero calls outgoing or incoming on trading Acuna."
Rangers 'intend to explore moving' SS Corey Seager

Texas will explore the possibility of trading star shortstop Corey Seager at the GM meetings, though Rosenthal notes that it would be a challenge, as the infielder is owed $155 million over the next five seasons at 33 years old. Seager also has full no-trade protection as a player with 10 years of service time, including five consecutive with the same club.
Seager has also had recent injury issues, including elbow surgery in 2026, an appendectomy last year and a sports hernia the year before.
Nationals' Dylan Crews has emerged as trade target
Washington outfielder Dylan Crews has become a trade target, with "a number of teams" expressing interest, per Nusbaum. The former No. 2 pick posted a .663 OPS in 2026.
'At least six' teams to meet with Skubal, including Padres, Blue Jays

According to Heyman, "at least six" teams have scheduled a meeting with star pitcher Tarik Skubal, including the Dodgers, Padres, Blue Jays and Mets. The process with Skubal is expected to move quickly after those meeting next week.
Tigers ink reliever Emilio Pagan on 1-year deal
Detroit is signing former Reds reliever Emilio Pagan to a one-year, $11 million deal. He posted a 3.38 ERA and 25 saves in 28 chances in 2026.
Mets schedule meeting with Tarik Skubal

The Mets have put a meeting with star pitcher Tarik Skubal on their calendar, per Heyman, as they consider an offer to the best player on the market. New York and the Dodgers have been considered the top players for Skubal, both with deep pockets to pull off a signing.

articles.headline: Jazz Chisholm Jr. signing with Blue Jays: Two-time All-Star staying in AL East on one-year deal, per reports
keyFacts: Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. agreed to a one-year, $20 million contract with the Toronto Blue Jays, according to reports.
Chisholm recorded 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases during the 2026 season while providing strong defense and baserunning.
The Blue Jays intend to play Chisholm at second base following their 83-loss season in 2026.
body: One of the most talented but also enigmatic free agents is heading to Toronto. The Blue Jays have agreed to a one-year contract with second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., reports ESPN. Fansided initially reported that the two sides were close. The deal is worth $20 million and includes a player option. The Blue Jays have not yet confirmed the news.

Chisholm is a year removed from a 31-homer, 31-steal, All-Star season with the New York Yankees, but his bat slipped badly in 2026, and he had his worst offensive season since his rookie year in 2021. He still managed 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases and has 30-30 upside, which the Blue Jays will surely hope to tap into next season.
, and the second-best position player. Here's the write-up:

In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.

The Yankees declined to give Chisholm the $23.15 million qualifying offer, signaling a split was on the horizon. They will not gain a compensation draft pick for losing him, nor will the American League East rival Blue Jays surrender a draft pick for signing him.

With the Jays, Chisholm figures to slot into his preferred position of second base. Last season, Ernie Clement was Toronto's primary at the position, but he struggled at the plate with an OPS+ of just 78 for the season. Clement figures to return to a utility role for manager John Schneider. Chisholm also has experience at third base, but coming off a 33-homer campaign, Kazuma Okamoto figures to retain that role in Toronto for 2027.

The Blue Jays claimed the pennant in 2025 and pushed the Los Angeles Dodgers to seven games in the World Series. Last season, however, they backslid to 83 losses and last place in the division. The offense was the key culprit for the Jays, and a rebound campaign for Chisholm would surely help matters. Not long ago, Toronto fortified the rotation with the free-agent addition of right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan.

articles.headline: Huge blow for Arsenal! David Raya misses training as doubts grow over his fitness for Manchester City showdown
keyFacts: Goalkeeper David Raya missed Arsenal training on Friday after injuring his shoulder during last weekend's match against Newcastle United, according to the Daily Mail.
Manager Mikel Arteta stated before the training session that there was still hope Raya could feature in Sunday's match against Manchester City.
Kepa Arrizabalaga is prepared to play in goal for Arsenal if Raya is not fit for the Premier League showdown.
body: Newcastle United v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport David Raya has missed Arsenal training, throwing his availability for Sunday's Premier League showdown with Manchester City into doubt. The goalkeeper has been sidelined since injuring his shoulder in last weekend's draw at Newcastle, and his absence comes just hours after Mikel Arteta suggested there was still hope he could feature at the Emirates.

Raya did not take part in Arsenal's training session on Friday, according to the Daily Mail . The Spaniard was forced off in the 70th minute of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle last Saturday after hurting his shoulder in an accidental collision with William Osula.

There were initial fears that Raya faced an extended spell on the sidelines, and Kepa Arrizabalaga started in his place in Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund. However, a scan showed the injury would not require surgery.

Arteta had been coy over the goalkeeper's fitness at his pre-match press conference earlier on Friday, before news of Raya's absence emerged. "I don't know. We still have a few hours before the game. We're just trying to get everyone back," he said.

Asked whether Raya was training, Arteta replied: "Yeah, they're all training." However, when asked if the goalkeeper was diving around, he said: "That, I'm not sure." The Arsenal boss also answered "yeah" when asked if there was hope Raya could be involved against Manchester City.

Raya's absence does not rule him out of Sunday's clash, but significant doubts remain over whether he will be fit in time for the visit of City. If he misses out, Kepa is set to deputise for Raya, who was recently hailed by John Terry as "the best keeper in the world" .

Arteta backed his deputy, saying: "The experience that Kepa has is incredible, and for the teams he's been involved, the trophies that he's won." Asked whether Sunday's starting goalkeeper would have a surname ending in A, he replied: "Probably."
Arsenal go into Sunday's clash six points ahead of Enzo Maresca's side, knowing victory would stretch the gap to nine points.
They will also be without Bukayo Saka, who is still expected to be out for another three weeks.

The staff sorted through thousands of discounts to highlight tested products, noting that prices are up in several categories due to RAMageddon.
The Verge stated that most deals are expected to stick around through the long holiday weekend.

You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.

As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge . With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price-hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.

Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review .

Who needs magnets when you have suction cups? Octobuddy’s cheap silicone mount works with most phones to provide hands-free flexibility whenever necessary. It features 24 single-sided cups, which allow you to stick your phone to a mirror, window, or any other surface you think will provide that perfect TikTok angle.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and DreamWorks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.
Fanttik X9 Pro Portable Tire Inflator

The Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150PSI.
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad follows up the 10th-gen model with a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

007 First Light , a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman , is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review .
Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
The cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design.

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review .

Acer’s answer to the MacBook Neo , with an Intel Core 5 processor, 8GB of RAM, 120Hz display, and speedy Thunderbolt 4 ports. We’re still testing this one, but it’s showing promise for an affordable choice.

Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary . And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.

Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review .

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.
The latest super-rugged wearable from Apple features better battery life than the previous version, plus AI-powered features like Siri Recap also available on the Series 12.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review .

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
$1499.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (with Dreame W10 vacuum)
Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.
TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review .

Roku now makes some of the most affordable yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on .
The best XPS 13 in years. It doesn’t have a headphone jack and starts with only 8GB of RAM but it’s an excellent thin-and-light with a great screen, a solid Intel chip, and speedy storage.

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review .

The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe , but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review .

Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.
It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review .

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review .

Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It also works with the new Aliro standard, making it compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking. Read our review.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

In Catan , up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge , especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.
Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees set

Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.

The Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.

Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review .

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible. Read our review.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review .

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan , but it is far more interesting.
A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.

The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Fairphone’s latest is a very light update to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.
Ugreen Nexode 240W USB-C Cable with Digital Display

The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.
The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon , part Minecraft , and part Animal Crossing . Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep mother dearest occupied for hours on end.

Google’s new Pixel 10A introduces faster wired charging, Satellite SOS, and new AI tools like Camera Coach and Auto Best Take. Otherwise, it’s basically the Pixel 9A, with the same Tensor G4 chip and a dual-camera system. Read our review .
The entry-point into RTX Spark laptops, the Asus ProArt is a creator-focused MacBook Pro wannabe with a sleek blacked-out design and lovely OLED display. Read our initial Nvidia RTX Spark hands-on .

There are many gaming headsets out there, but few as elegant as Fractal’s Scape. The PC-focused (but Switch- and PlayStation-compatible) wireless headset offer great sound and include a wireless charger, and they have easy-to-master physical controls.

Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

Govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 are Matter-ready smart lights you can leave up year-round. They can display multiple colors at once, with 100 preset lighting scenes, customizable effects, and the ability to sync to music. The lights also feature an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.

The Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is an excellent option for adding smarts and some style to your HVAC system. As well as being a smart way to control your energy use, the thermostat can also act as a video intercom for Ecobee’s excellent doorbell camera and an indoor air quality monitor. Read our review.

The Cricut Joy 2 is a small crafting machine designed for smaller projects, including custom cards, stickers, vinyl decals, labels, bookmarks, and iron-ons. It can cut designs up to 4.5 inches wide and brings Cricut’s Print Then Cut feature to its entry-level lineup. Read our review .
$199 $139 at Cricut (150-project bundle and one-month subscription)

Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.

Although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to.
Update, November 27th: Updated to include several new picks, including those for the Cricut Joy 2, Apple Pencil (USB-C), and the Echo Time.

articles.headline: The super-thin-and-light, but pricey foldable is available for an almost unbelievable Black Friday deal price
keyFacts: Samsung is offering Black Friday discounts in the US on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, including up to $1,100 off through trade-ins and price cuts.
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra features an 8-inch internal display, a 200MP main camera, and a lighter design compared to competing devices.
Buyers can also receive upfront discounts and additional savings using coupons and specific payment codes during the sale.
body: In the battle of the best foldable phones, the ultra-light, thin, and visibly flat (when unfolded) Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is almost unbeatable, and now you can, in the US, get almost $1,100 off the $2,099.99 starting price from Samsung.

The deal is a mixture of a price cut, coupons, and trade-ins (with values of up to $800 off), but if you have an old Samsung (or other brand) lying around, it's certainly a Black Friday deal worth looking into.

I won't argue that paying over $2k for any phone is a stretch, though I've long argued that these foldables are true two-in-one devices; more specifically, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is an excellent example of the species.
Yes, even in the face of the new iPhone Duo (impressive, yes, but there's no Black Friday deal for it in sight), the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is notable.

As I wrote in my review, "it still reigns supreme". Here's why. Not only is it thinner and lighter than Samsung's own Galaxy S26 Ultra flagship (which also has a nice Black Friday deal), but the unfolding Z Fold 8 Ultra is roughly 40 grams lighter than the iPhone Duo.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: $350 off upfront, or up to $1100 off with a trade-in

Samsung's Black Friday deals on its latest foldable devices are incredibly strong if you're looking for a discount on an unlocked device. First up, you can get up to $800 off via a trade-in rebate on either the Fold 8 or Ultra, and up to $400 off the Flip 8. If that doesn't suit, then you can instead get an upfront discount of up to $350 off, which really helps offset the cost of these pricey premium devices.
Galaxy Z Fold 8: $300 off upfront, or up to $800 off w/ trade
Galaxy Z Flip 8: $200 off upfront, or up to $400 off w/ trade
Is the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra really all that ultra?

It also has a better main camera, which specs out to 200MP wide, which is backed up by a 50MP wide and a 3x 10MP telephoto cameras. By contrast, the passport-shaped Galaxy Z Fold 8 (also sporting a Black Friday deal of its own) has just two cameras on the back (both are 50MP). Even the new iPhone Duo can only muster two 48MP cameras.

One thing I always loved about the Z Fold 8 Ultra is that, folded, it feels like you're carrying a svelte flagship phone but with a hidden secret: the 8-inch internal display. Yes, I wish it accepted pen input (like the iPhone Duo) and that Samsung would quickly adopt the Duo's crease-erasing nanotexture main display covering, but I still think this is a virtually unbeatable deal, and now, at this Black Friday Deal, it's well worth the price of entry.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: $350 off upfront, or up to $720 off with a trade-in at Samsung

The outstanding Galaxy S26 Ultra has just been listed for its lowest price yet at the official Samsung Store this week, with an excellent $350 discount on unlocked devices. Available across all storage variants and colors, this deal can get you a device for as little as $949 upfront. Trade-in rebates of up to $720 are also available, but we've seen slightly better offerings in the past for trades.
Galaxy S26: $150 off upfront, or up to $340 off w/ trade
Galaxy S26+: $250 off upfront, or up to $440 off w/ trade

To cut the price of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra virtually in half this Black Friday, you will need a trade-in that could garner you up to $800 off. Without one, you're looking at $450 off. You can also pick up a few hundred more off with a PayPal code (PAYPAL100) and then an additional $200 off in coupon deals.

Seriously, though, getting a decent trade-in on your old traditional flagship smartphone should be considered a win when you're getting a 6.5-inch smartphone with an additional, multitasking-reading 8-inch flexible display. That's truly a tablet and phone in one lightweight, fully-pocketable device.

The upgrades from the Galaxy Z Fold 7 Ultra weren't major, but as I wrote in my review: "Samsung has upgraded it just enough — it's flatter, lighter, and has a better battery and better cameras," and now it's an even better value than you might think.

articles.headline: Jaguars get bad news on Bhayshul Tuten for Week 12 amid ankle and foot injuries
keyFacts: The Jacksonville Jaguars ruled out running back Bhayshul Tuten and wide receiver Parker Washington for their Week 12 game against the Tennessee Titans.
Mia O'Brien of ESPN reported that Tuten is sidelined due to ankle and foot injuries, while Washington is dealing with a shoulder injury.
The Jaguars will rely on Chris Rodriguez Jr., LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah to fill the running back position in Tuten's absence.
body: As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepared for their Week 12 matchup against the Tennessee Titans, coming off a loss to the New York Giants in Week 11, they're dealing with two key injury issues on their offense.

Parker Washington suffered an AC joint injury during practice and has been ruled out for Week 12. There's a chance he misses more time, but for now, he's out for Week 12. Unfortunately, he's not the only offensive starter set to miss time this week.
According to Mia O'Brien of ESPN, the Jaguars have also ruled out running back Bhayshul Tuten for Week 12, as the breakout sophomore RB is dealing with ankle and foot injury issues.
Jaguars rule out Bhayshul Tuten for Week 12 amid two injury issues
"Jaguars have officially ruled Bhayshul Tuten and Parker Washington OUT vs Titans," O'Brien reported Friday afternoon.
Tuten has been a big piece of the offense in Jacksonville this year, and now he's going to miss a week due to a combination of ankle and foot injury issues.

The Jaguars, sitting at 7-3 and set to face the 1-9 Titans this week, will be down their two best offensive playmakers. Washington, the breakout WR, is out with a shoulder issue, and Tuten, the breakout RB, is out with ankle and foot injuries.
After 11 weeks, Tuten has 158 rushing attempts for 642 yards and five touchdowns. He also has 21 receptions for 226 yards and three touchdowns in the passing game.
Losing him is a big loss, and the only reason it's not a lot worse is that the Jaguars are facing a weaker Titans team this week.
In Tuten's place, the Jaguars will be leaning on running back Chris Rodriguez Jr., along with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.
Rodriguez should be the lead back, with Abdullah and Allen factoring into the offense on passing downs and in two-minute drills.

The Jaguars will be without Bhayshul Tuten and Parker Washington in Week 12, as the offense will be short-handed against the Titans in an important divisional matchup for Jacksonville coming off a tough loss in Week 11.

articles.headline: 8 New TV Shows to Watch This Weekend on Netflix and Prime Video (November 27-29)
keyFacts: Polygon released a list of eight new television shows available to stream on Netflix and Prime Video over the weekend.
New and returning titles featured include Blade Runner: 2099, The Hunting Wives, Always on Call, and Fool Night.
Other additions to streaming platforms feature the documentary series The Trials of Karen Read and The Great British Baking Show: Holidays.
body: Happy Thanksgiving! There’s a lot of TV to watch this weekend, whether you’re tuning in to shows that are already airing or looking for your next binge.

The Rings of Power has been releasing new episodes on Tuesdays, with the finale airing on Nov. 24 (be sure to check out our Sauron explainer). We’re also covering new episodes of Yellowjackets, which air on Fridays (The series premiere revealed one of its biggest mysteries).

When it comes to new offerings, there’s plenty of exciting stuff. Blade Runner: 2099 premiered this Wednesday, set in a new world where Replicants have replaced humans as the world’s dominant force. If you’re looking for something juicy and bingeable and very awkward for family viewing, The Hunting Wives just premiered its sophomore season, depicting more murders in Texas.
There are plenty of international TV shows this week, including Always on Call and Fool Night, with some anime and reality TV shows newly available to stream. Happy watching!
- Cast: Hunter Schafer, Michelle Yeoh, Katelyn Rose Downey

Set 50 years after Blade Runner: 2049, the series completely shuffles things around. After exploring the dynamics with humans and replicants in two beloved films, the new TV show finds humans as the underclass. The story follows Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human on the run pretending to be a Blade Runner in order to secure a future for herself and her brother.

While Blade Runner 2049 was a direct sequel that continued the story of Harrison Ford’s Rick Deckard, Blade Runner 2099 creator and showrunner Silka Luisa focuses more on exploring the franchise’s themes than advancing its plot. Fifty years after the events of the 2017 film, the Replicants once used as slave labor out in space have led an uprising and now rule Los Angeles. Rather than searching for rogue Replicants, Blade Runners brutally enforce order amongst the humans unlucky enough to be trapped on the barely habitable planet. Desperate human fugitive Cora (Hunter Schafer) is offered a chance at a fresh start if she can impersonate a Replicant to steal something from the police evidence room. When Cora discovers a rogue Blade Runner already took her prize, she has to team up with his former partner Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) to find it.
- Cast: Malin Akerman, Brittany Snow, Dermot Mulroney

The Netflix overnight phenomenon The Hunting Wives is back for a second season, building on the first season and novel. This time around, the show is telling an original story, continuing the tale that was first laid out by the book. The new season finds Sophie (Brittany Snow) at a turning point: she killed Margo’s (Malin Akerman) brother, leaving her with another secret to hide amid their complicated relationship.
- Cast: Sara Khorami, Thorbjørn Harr, Silje Storstein

If you're into Norwegian dramas, Always on Call is now on Netflix. The Norwegian series follows a surgeon who has just started working at an overwhelmed emergency room that serves as a last resort. Each episode explores new cases and workplace medical drama that continues to satisfy viewers of all sorts.
- Cast: Koki Uchiyama, Minako Kotobuki, Junya Enoki

Netflix’s new dystopian anime is set in a world without sunlight, where humanity relies on an optional medical intervention called transfloration. Volunteers are paid handsomely to have a flower implanted in them; it blooms two years later and provides oxygen for others. The series follows an impoverished boy who agrees to the procedure, gaining an ability that allows him to hear the voices of Spiriflora. He soon finds himself drawn into a complex conspiracy.

Based on the manga by Kasumi Yasuda and directed by Atsuyuki Yukawa, Fool Night is a surprisingly intimate story set against an enormous environmental catastrophe. Rather than throwing viewers into an expansive science fiction mystery, Yukawa takes his time introducing its main characters and how their lives become intertwined by circumstances neither could have anticipated. It's a more methodical introduction than some might expect, offering plenty of room to establish the people at the center of a world literally steeped in darkness and comforted only by the discarded remains of the volunteers transformed into grotesque flora.

Netflix’s new three-part documentary series explores the death of police officer John O’Keefe and the case against his girlfriend, Karen Read, who was believed to be the prime suspect. She faced two murder trials.

Netflix’s latest reality TV competition follows Salish Matter, a YouTube star who invites seven of her closest friends to a snow-covered getaway for holiday-themed party games. But, since this is 2026 and things can't be that simple, there's an impostor in the group, whose mission is to sabotage all challenges and steal the gifts without anyone else noticing it.
7 The Great British Baking Show: Holidays

Netflix’s staple holiday cooking series is back with two new episodes. The Great British Baking Show: Holidays is a spin-off of the beloved cooking show, with previous competitors returning for a season themed around Christmas and New Year’s Day.
- Cast: Nobuhiko Okamoto, Kana Hanazawa, Yuki Kaji

Blue Exorcist follows a teen raised by an exorcist priest who discovers he's the son of Satan and a human woman. His journey of vengeance against his father begins when Satan tries to claim him as a vessel, with the priest and caretaker sacrificing himself to protect him. The series’ third season is now available on Netflix.

Any shōnen that leverages religious mythology and symbolism to flesh out its world-building is already off to a great start, and Blue Exorcist makes good use of this premise. Two mirror dimensions exist: Assiah, the material world for humans, and Gehenna, the demonic realm ruled by Satan. The demons often breach through the earthly realm via human possession, which is why we have Exorcists, who secretly work for the Vatican and take down these threats. Our protagonist is Rin Okamura (and to an extent, his twin Yukio), who learn that they’re sons of Satan after witnessing their human father’s death.

articles.headline: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
keyFacts: Spanish party leaders, including Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo, held final campaign rallies ahead of Sunday's election.
Polls show the People's Party narrowly leading, with leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo seeking parliamentary support from the anti-immigration party Vox.
Almost 39 million voters will decide the election on Sunday, which commentators and polls indicate will be a close finish.
body: Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.
"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for selfies with supporters in red T-shirts and accusing conservative rival Alberto NÃºÃ±ez FeijÃ³o of planning a coalition with the far right.

FeijÃ³o's People's Party (PP) is narrowly ahead in the polls, and in the final hours of the campaign he travelled first to Barcelona and then Seville, promising voters a new political era of "truth, decency and good governance".
He accused SÃ¡nchez of evading questions on key issues like corruption, rail disasters, immigration and the national debt.

The Socialist leader heads one of Europe's few left-wing governments, and with the French presidential elections five months away, there is a real chance that two of the continent's biggest economies could move to the right in quick succession.

Almost 39 million people have a vote in Spain and while commentators expect a high turnout, most polls have suggested a close finish. Under Spanish electoral law, no polls have been published since Monday.
"This time, yes, we're going to do it," FeijÃ³o told PP supporters, in a nod to his failure to form a government three years ago despite winning most seats.

If he gets to form a government this time, it will be with the support of anti-immigration party Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, whose final rally took place in front of thousands of people in a bull-ring in Valencia on Spain's east coast.
The venue was filled with Spanish flags and green Vox banners, and one of the biggest cheers of the night came when the secretary general of the party called for "less burka and less halal".
Ignacio Garriga said he was not acting out of hatred but love for the homeland.
A small section of the crowd could be heard chanting "Viva Franco" in reference to the dictator, whose death in 1975 heralded the start of Spain's transition to democracy.
A number of first-time voters at the rally said they were supporting Vox because of its policies on immigration.

LledÃ³, 18, said what had happened in Ceuta in the summer, when more than 70,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco, showed SÃ¡nchez was not able to control the country's border.
She had come to the bullring with her mum and aunt, Carli Chilet, who argued that Vox "are the best for women's rights".

Vox is hoping to almost double its seats from the 33 it won three years ago. It backs policies such as "national priority" - putting Spanish citizens first for welfare - and "remigration" for foreigners not considered to be contributing to the economy.
The final day of campaigning was very much in the shadow of a four-way TV debate the night before that exposed Spain's sharply polarised politics.

All four leaders had solutions for the housing crisis. FeijÃ³o said the PP would build a million homes over four years, while SÃ¡nchez said housing should be a right not an object of speculation and profit.

While the conservatives tried to turn the spotlight on the series of scandals that have overshadowed the Socialists' term in office, SÃ¡nchez and his left-wing ally Ada Colau, who heads Frente Amplio (The Broad Front), focused on women's rights.

The two leaders seized on a moment in the debate when the PP leader accused Colau and the rest of the left of staying quiet during a flood disaster in Valencia, briefly moving his finger to his lips. The word he used "calladita" is a diminutive and can also be used to tell a woman to "keep quiet" in a condescending manner.
SÃ¡nchez reacted immediately and called on him to show "a little respect", accusing him of sexism.

FeijÃ³o sought to clarify what he meant on Friday, and accused Ada Colau of remaining silent during "these years of corruption". His decision to wind up his campaign in Seville was significant, because the wider southern region of Andalusia has 61 seats in Spain's 350-seat parliament, more than any other.
Andalusia is also important because it is run by a coalition made up of the PP and Abascal's Vox, as are three other regions, Extremadura, AragÃ³n, and Castilla y LeÃ³n.
FeijÃ³o has insisted he wants to govern with a majority, backed up by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox and says he has never spoken to Abascal about giving Vox ministerial power.
SÃ¡nchez took to the stage in Madrid with his wife BegoÃ±a GÃ³mez, and donned a red T-shirt that read "power of the people".

He then went on to praise Colau and her left-wing coalition's campaign. As he was speaking, Colau told a large audience in the south of Madrid that not only would they "not remain silent, we will win", vowing to form another "progressive government".

articles.headline: 25-year sentence sought for former chef who aided 14 suicides
keyFacts: Canadian prosecutors requested a 25-year prison sentence for Kenneth Law for selling poison online to assist suicides.
Law sold lethal sodium nitrite to people in at least 41 countries, Canadian prosecutors said.
The judge is expected to make a final sentencing decision over the coming weeks.
body: Canadian prosecutors on Friday requested a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold poison to help people die by suicide, stressing his victims were largely young and experiencing mental distress.
Former chef Kenneth Law earlier this year to aiding in Canada, but he has admitted to selling his so-called suicide kits through a series of online forums.
Prosecutors had also charged him with murder but, citing a lack of evidence, agreed to withdraw the more serious accusations in exchange for Law pleading guilty to lesser offenses.
That decision , notably from friends and family of victims who believed Law was directly responsible for killing their loved ones, but prosecutors maintained they would still seek a stiff penalty.
"An appropriate global sentence to impose in this matter is 25 years less (time already served)," Crown prosecutor Katie Doherty told the court.
Courts often use comparable cases in determining sentencing, but Doherty noted there is "no case even remotely similar to Mr Law's conduct."
The Canadian public was shocked when the breadth of Law's operation was revealed following his arrest.

He sold poison to people in at least 41 countries, including China, France, and Brazil. He sold 330 packages to people in the United Kingdom, according to an agreed statement of facts signed by the defense and prosecution. There, 79 deaths are linked to him, according to Canadian prosecutors.

He admitted to entering suicide chat forums under an alias, identifying people considering ending their lives and then directing them to one of his online shops where he sold lethal concentrations of the meat preservative sodium nitrite.
In 2023, Canadian police released photos of the sodium nitrite, adding that a joint operation led by 11 police agencies from across Ontario were investigating the case.
"Investigators are asking members of the community to be alert of any packaging or label identifying sodium nitrite," Constable Sarah Patten said at the time.
Law, who was born in 1965, sold poison to people who were "just starting off their lives" and "battling mental illness," Doherty said.
That is "a very significant aggravating factor in this case," Doherty said.
The judge is expected to make a final sentencing decision over the coming weeks.
Prosecutors in the U.K. decided not to charge Law despite for dozens of deaths.
The Crown Prosecution Service and the National Crime Agency said they had decided Law "should be sentenced for the full extent of his offending within a single sentencing process in Canada."
In a letter to bereaved families, the organizations said it had been a "difficult decision."
"No outcome in any court can remove the pain victims and their families have suffered," they said.
