articles.headline: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds a Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
keyFacts: TORONTO (AP) — Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld most of a Quebec law banning public schoolteachers, police officers and other public employees in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols at work.
The ruling affirmed Quebec's power to override certain constitutional rights to keep the ban in place.
The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.
body: TORONTO (AP) — Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld most of a Quebec law banning public schoolteachers, police officers and other public employees in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols at work. The ruling affirmed Quebec's power to override certain constitutional rights to keep the ban in place.
The 2019 law, known as Bill 21, bans religious symbols — including Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses — for workers covered by it.

Canada has long embraced multiculturalism, encouraging people to retain their cultural and religious identities. Supporters of Quebec's ban say public officials should avoid wearing religious symbols to demonstrate government neutrality.
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon welcomed the ruling as "a victory for secularism" and for Quebec's ability to make different choices from the rest of Canada.

The court upheld Quebec's use of the "notwithstanding clause," which allows lawmakers to override certain rights, including religious freedom and equality. Those rights are protected by the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, Canada's equivalent of the U.S. Bill of Rights. Lawmakers must renew the override every five years to keep it in effect.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said he respected the ruling but pledged that his government would not use the constitutional override. He stressed that constitutional rights are particularly important for minorities and vulnerable people.
"Canada is a mosaic," Carney said, adding that it represents more than different backgrounds and identities. "It's a commitment, in my judgment, a commitment to how we treat each other."

Carney also welcomed the court's finding that judges can still declare that a law violates constitutional rights even when the override allows it to remain in force. He said that scrutiny helps inform Canadians and is useful in a democracy.
Chief Justice Richard Wagner wrote that the law reflected Quebec's "legitimate and historical commitment" to keeping government secular.
The court maintained an exemption allowing members of Quebec's legislature to cover their heads — or potentially, for women, to cover their faces — while performing their duties.
Quebec's commitment to secularism grew from its rejection of the Roman Catholic Church's once-dominant influence.
Opponents say the law discriminates against religious minorities, particularly Muslim women who wear headscarves.
"Quebec is still telling qualified people that they must set aside their faith," said Mehramat Kaur of the World Sikh Organization of Canada.
France, Belgium, Austria and the Netherlands have full or partial bans on face coverings, including veils worn by some Muslim women.
Other Canadian provinces have used the override for laws restricting transgender rights or ordering striking employees back to work.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew called Bill 21 "legislated discrimination" against Muslims, Sikhs and other religious minorities. He said his government would never use the override.
"If I need to pick on somebody in order to get elected, I don't deserve the office," Kinew said.

articles.headline: Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office
keyFacts: National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez announced that Venezuela will repeal a 2024 law that bans opposition figures from holding office.
The repeal stems from political transition talks between the US-backed interim government and selected members of the opposition.
Meanwhile, opposition leader Maria Corina Machado launched neighbourhood assemblies to gather proposals for a future democratic transition.
body: Venezuela will repeal a law that prohibits opposition figures from office, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez has announced.
The legislation, approved in 2024 and criticised for enabling political persecution, targeted those who promoted or supported sanctions against the country.
“That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through,” Rodriguez said on Thursday.
The law was passed just after fraught elections which the then-incumbent Nicolas Maduro ultimately won amid widespread allegations of fraud.

An interim government headed by Delcy Rodriguez, the parliamentary chief’s sister, has run Venezuela since Maduro’s abduction by US forces in January. Delcy Rodriguez promised in September during a speech at the United Nations that the South American country will hold free and fair elections, without setting a date.

Since then, the US-backed government has been in political transition talks with parts of the opposition selected by Washington. That dialogue had reached an agreement to review several laws, including the one up for repeal now, according to Jorge Rodriguez.

Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado shook up Venezuelan politics with her surprise return from exile last month. Machado won an opposition primary in 2023 to take on Maduro in the following year’s election, but she was legally barred from running. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate is widely expected to run for office in the event of an election, despite her exclusion from transition talks.

Despite being shut out, on Thursday Machado launched a system of neighbourhood assemblies aiming to gather proposals for a future government programme and democratic transition. The assemblies are expected to bring together over a million people over several months, according to Machado’s team.

“We listened to neighbours who are breaking down barriers that many thought were impossible, debating the issues that will lay the foundations for the Venezuela to come,” Machado said on social media on Thursday after the meetings. “We are designing the transition to democracy, the Venezuelan way.”
Around 2,000 meetings with residents were organised in Venezuela and abroad on the first day of the initiative, her team told the AFP news agency.

Nineteen questions are asked during the assembly, with responses fed into a digital platform. Issues of national interest range from dates for the presidential election to changes in the justice, education, health, wage and pension systems, as well as the role of the public and private sectors.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear arguments on AR-15 bans in huge Second Amendment case
keyFacts: The US Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on December 2 regarding state and local bans on assault-style rifles.
The proceedings involve challenges to firearm bans passed in Connecticut and Chicago's Cook County.
The Supreme Court will decide whether states and localities retain the authority to ban these semiautomatic weapons.
body: WASHINGTON — The US Supreme Court will hear arguments next week on state and local bans of so-called “assault-style” rifles like the AR-15.

The Dec. 2 oral arguments come after victims’ families of the mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Conn., appealed to the high court to uphold prohibitions on certain semiautomatic rifles.

A lone gunman massacred 20 first graders and six educators in the 2012 shooting — and the Supreme Court will now get to decide whether to allow localities or states the ability to ban the powerful firearms.
The court is hearing challenges in two cases — one against a Connecticut law and the other involving a ban passed in Chicago’s Cook County in the 1990s.

“The basic function of government is to keep its citizenry safe, and these guns are so incredibly dangerous in a densely populated area like Chicago,” Cook County State’s Attorney Eileen O’Neill Burke (D) told CNN. “One hundred percent of the children who were hit with this weapon at Sandy Hook died.”
In the past, bills pushing for bans of assault weapons have been unable to pass both chambers of Congress.
In the Connecticut and Cook County cases, lawyers are making use of the high court’s reasoning in a 2022 decision: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen.
In a brief written ahead of Wednesday’s arguments, lawyers defending Connecticut’s ban passed in the wake of the Sandy Hook shooting invoked that tradition.

“From fourteenth-century England to twenty-first century America, governments have restricted weapons because of their unusually dangerous properties,” they wrote. “In each instance, legislatures have determined that a weapon is atypically lethal relative to its peers — and so have acted to prevent that weapon’s use.”
There are also arguments made in the briefs that the AR-15 assault rifle in particular has links to military-style weapons like the M16.
Start your day with all you need to know
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
Almost a dozen states have passed similar assault weapon-style bans, as well as Washington, DC. A federal ban on the weapons and high-capacity magazines expired in 2004.
Past court decisions from some in the conservative supermajority could indicate which way justices are leaning on the issue.

Justices Clarence Thomas, Samuel Alito and Brett Kavanaugh have dissented from past decisions by the court to not take up challenges to the assault-style rifle bans — or dissented in their roles on appeals courts from rulings upholding the bans.
It’s unclear whether similarly conservative Justices Neil Gorsuch, Amy Coney Barrett or John Roberts will have similar opinions.

articles.headline: Marvel's Iron Man might be planning to rear its head at The Game Awards, if EA Motive's updated website is any indication
keyFacts: Redditors noticed that EA Motive updated its official website ahead of The Game Awards.
Disney announced that viewers can expect major gaming announcements during the ceremony airing on December 10.
An unfinished trailer for the Iron Man game leaked on the internet this summer.
body: EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.

Redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.
A new website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

For one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio said earlier this month.
Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

Second is the fact that The Game Awards air on 10th December - eight days before the global opening of Avengers: Doomsday, a film that's shaping up to become the biggest cinematic event since the last time Marvel chucked all of its toys into the same sandbox and bashed them together. Giving one of the company's most popular superheroes the spotlight around the same time seems like a good idea.

This isn't the first time EA's Iron Man has popped up in recent times, either. What appeared to be an unfinished trailer for Motive's Iron Man leaked onto the internet this summer, and showed off blisteringly fast flying and lots of destructive gadgets. It looked further along than I expected, at least, so I wouldn't be surprised to see the billionaire playboy philanthropist rear his head again in two weeks time.

articles.headline: From ‘Star Trek’ to NASA: Pamela Melroy’s American dream
keyFacts: Retired astronaut Pamela Melroy discussed her career as an Air Force pilot and NASA leader in an interview with the Washington Examiner.
Melroy said watching Apollo 11 and policy changes allowing female military pilots enabled her to pursue spaceflight.
Melroy stated that perseverance and her education at Wellesley College helped her overcome skepticism in male-dominated aviation fields.
body: For retired Air Force Col. Pamela Melroy, the American dream is more than an ideal. It is a promise of opportunity that helped take her from a childhood fascination with space to the cockpit of a NASA space shuttle.

In an interview with Washington Examiner’s Bob Cusack as part of the America at 250 series, Melroy reflected on the opportunities that shaped her life, the obstacles she overcame, and the American values that made her extraordinary journey possible.
Melroy, who flew three space shuttle missions and later served as NASA’s deputy administrator, credited America with giving her the freedom and opportunity to pursue her dreams.

“The idea that a little girl could grow up in the ’60s, very different time, and become an Air Force test pilot, but even more importantly, become an astronaut, that would never happen in any other country,” Melroy said
From watching ‘Star Trek’ to reaching for the stars
Melroy’s fascination with space began long before she entered a cockpit.

Born while her father was pursuing a master’s degree in computer science at Stanford University, Melroy grew up in a household that encouraged curiosity and imagination. Every Friday night, her family gathered to watch Star Trek, introducing her to a world of exploration and seemingly limitless possibilities.
But it was watching the Apollo 11 moon landing that transformed her fascination into a personal ambition.
“I’m seeing men walking on the moon. And I’m like, wait, you mean I could have that for a job?” she said.
Her parents instilled in her the confidence to pursue whatever career she wanted, regardless of the expectations society placed on young women at the time.
While she was in high school, women became eligible to serve as military pilots, opening a pathway that would eventually lead her to the Air Force, NASA, and outer space.
Breaking barriers with courage and perseverance
Melroy’s journey was not without challenges. Entering professions historically dominated by men, she encountered skepticism about her abilities and faced obstacles that tested her determination.

Rather than allowing those experiences to discourage her, Melroy chose to approach them with confidence, kindness, and humor. She recalled how she would respond when fellow pilots expressed uncertainty about flying with a woman.
“Things like, well, I’ve never flown with a woman before. So I’d say I’ve flown with lots of guys, I’ll show you how it’s done,” she said. “It sort of takes the wind out of their sails.”
Her approach reflected a belief that perseverance and professionalism could help overcome prejudice and challenge assumptions.

With relatively few women having preceded her in military aviation and space exploration, Melroy had limited access to female mentors in those fields. However, she found inspiration during her time at Wellesley College, which she chose for its astronomy department. There, she was surrounded by women whose accomplishments challenged conventional expectations.
“When people say, ‘Hey, girls can’t do math and science,’ I was surrounded by role models that were proving that differently,” she said.
Those experiences reinforced her belief in the importance of education, opportunity, and confidence to pursue ambitions others might consider impossible.
The American dream and the next generation
Melroy’s remarkable journey embodies many of the enduring values at the heart of the Washington Examiner’s America at 250 project: courage, perseverance, freedom, equality, and opportunity.
Her story is a reminder of what becomes possible when individuals are encouraged to dream beyond conventional boundaries and given the opportunity to turn those dreams into reality.

As the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary, Melroy’s experiences offer an inspiring perspective on how far the nation has come and the importance of preserving opportunities for future generations of explorers, innovators, and leaders.
She concluded her conversation with a simple but heartfelt message to the country she credits with making her dreams possible.

articles.headline: 'A bit strange' - Leclerc seeking outlier to catch Mercedes in Qatar

body: Charles Leclerc seeking outlier as Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull try to catch Mercedes at Qatar Grand Prix

Mercedes dominated Friday's practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix and Charles Leclerc suggested Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull are missing something; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead of Qualifying at 6pm on Saturday live on Sky Sports F1
Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.
Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell.

Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.

Mercedes' dominance was similar to their pace advantage earlier in the season but the second half of 2026 has largely been very close between F1's top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.
Ferrari were over one second behind Antonelli on a dismal Friday as Leclerc spun in second practice and Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine problem which brought his Ferrari to a halt.
"Honestly it's been a very difficult day. It's not that we didn't try on the softs, we couldn't improve our lap time on the mediums," said Leclerc.
"I lost the car and had some damage so we had to repair the car but that was the first lap of FP2 and I couldn't improve and even on the new soft later on I couldn't improve.

"A very, very difficult day. The feeling is just very difficult to get right. Not even on high fuel we were strong, so for now, it looks like a very difficult weekend but we are working hard to try and understand something.
"For some reason, Mercedes are so much faster than everybody expected, so the gaps are just a little bit strange, so there's something that's an outlier and we just need to find that."

Ferrari were not expected to be strong at the Lusail International Circuit due to the long flat out zones and high-speed corners but Leclerc suggested his team, along with McLaren and Red Bull were missing a trick that will give them more pace.
"I don't think we know yet what's the outlier. I think other teams probably didn't find that because Mercedes still have a massive advantage," he said.
"We are going to work towards that and analyse the data to understand what's going on."
Norris: Mercedes not even worth thinking about
McLaren were predicted to be very competitive in Qatar due to their strength in the high-speed corners but Norris and Piastri were never close to matching the pace of Mercedes.

On Saturday, McLaren are expected to put the new floor they ran in Las Vegas on the car but Norris does not think it will make a big enouch difference to catch Mercedes who are in "a different category".
"I don't know how much that will help around here compared to Vegas," said last year's world champion.
"But obviously tonight [Friday] we will see how much we can gain from that. It's not going to be the gap we need.

"We are probably seven tenths off the Mercedes a lap so it's not even worth thinking about them. But relative to the rest we seem to be in a good place. The fact we can have the new floor on tomorrow will add a little bit and a little bit is better than nothing. We seem in a relatively decent place."
Both Antonelli and Russell pointed out that Verstappen will always be a threat and the four-time world champion is coy about his chances of challenging the Mercedes in qualifying.
"A bit of a difficult day. The balance of the car is a bit too disconnected at the moment to go fast, so that's what we need to fix," said the Red Bull driver.
"The all-round balance is not there at the moment and is costing us quite a bit of lap time. We will keep trying and see how good we can get it."
"Mercedes look quite far ahead on the short run and long run. Let's see how much we can close the gap."

RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. articles.headline: How parents can claim SpaceX stock after Elon Musk promises billions for kids’ Trump Accounts
keyFacts: Elon Musk and SpaceX pledged two shares of company stock per American child through Trump Accounts, valued at nearly $18 billion.
Parents must download the Trump Accounts app or visit TrumpAccounts.gov, verify their identity, and provide their child's information to claim the shares.
The IRS began automatically enrolling eligible children on October 1, and parents can also separately request a $1,000 federal pilot contribution.
body: Elon Musk is putting his money where his mouth is — pledging billions of dollars in SpaceX stock to American children through President Trump’s new savings program, but parents will need to take action to make sure their kids can benefit.

The tech billionaire and SpaceX announced this week that they would each donate one share of the rocket company’s stock to every child in the US through Trump Accounts, potentially giving millions of youngsters a stake in one of the world’s most valuable companies.
The combined giveaway is valued at nearly $18 billion based on SpaceX’s latest stock price, according to reports.
Musk doubled down on the pledge Thursday, writing on X: “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally.”
The massive commitment comes on top of more than $9 billion already deposited into Trump Accounts, according to the Treasury Department.

More than 3 million friends and family members have contributed over $1 billion to the accounts, while philanthropic donations — including major gifts from Michael and Susan Dell — and the federal government’s $1,000 seed contributions have helped push the total past $9 billion.
Musk’s newly announced stock pledge is separate from that existing total.
SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell has also pledged more than 2 million shares of the company’s stock to children through the program.

Shotwell announced in October that she and her husband would donate the shares, with an initial distribution targeting children ages 11 to 17 living in zip codes with median household incomes of $57,000 or less. Children in zip codes without sufficient income data would also qualify.
Parents can download the Trump Accounts app through the Apple App Store or Google Play, or visit the program’s website at TrumpAccounts.gov to get started.
An authorized parent or guardian must verify their identity and demonstrate they have the authority to manage the child’s account.

Parents should have their child’s legal name, date of birth and valid Social Security number handy, along with their own identifying information. The IRS advises families to make sure the details match Social Security Administration records to avoid delays.

Follow the instructions in the app or on the website to claim and activate the account. Even if the Treasury Department has automatically opened an account for an eligible child, parents must still claim it before they can manage it.

The IRS began automatically enrolling eligible children in Trump Accounts on Oct. 1. Children under 18 with valid Social Security numbers can qualify, even if they are not eligible for the separate federal seed contribution.
Parents should also know that the government offers a one-time $1,000 contribution to eligible US citizen children born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028.
That payment is not automatic. Parents must separately request it by submitting IRS Form 4547 and selecting the $1,000 pilot program contribution option.
The form can be submitted through the Trump Accounts app, the program’s website or an IRS online account.

articles.headline: Samsung is reportedly giving its camera app an AI mode
keyFacts: Samsung is reportedly adding a new Vision AI mode to its camera app for next year's Galaxy S27 devices, according to code strings found in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 by Android Authority.
The Vision mode will allow users to point their camera at objects to receive AI-written summaries, suggested actions, translation, and integration with Gemini and Bixby Vision.
Samsung has not officially announced the feature, and if launched, it will likely debut alongside the Galaxy S27 lineup early next year.
body: Samsung is reportedly giving its camera app an AI mode
The feature could mirror the Siri mode Apple added in iOS 27.

Samsung's Galaxy S26 phones already ship with Google's Android AI features and Perplexity, and the phone maker is reportedly layering in even more AI for next year's Galaxy S27 devices. Based on code strings in One UI 9.5 Beta 1, Android Authority writes that Samsung is adding a new "Vision" mode to Galaxy phones' camera app that could duplicate some of the use cases for Siri mode in iOS 27.

Vision will apparently be offered alongside the app's other modes, and primarily acts as a way to point your camera at something and ask AI about it. According to Android Authority, the camera mode will display an AI-written summary of whatever you're looking at, along with tappable keywords, suggested actions, a text extraction tool, an "Ask" button that sends the scene to Gemini and a "Translate" button that hands it off to Samsung's AI Vision app.

Samsung's phones already offer a way to open Google's Gemini Live feature to have a live conversation about whatever you're looking at, and even before that, Samsung experimented with multimodal AI features through Bixby. Funnily enough, Android Authority writes that the AI Vision app this new camera feature connects to is actually built on the bones of Bixby Vision, the camera capabilities of Samsung's in-house AI assistant.

Vision also sounds similar to the Siri mode Apple added to the Camera app in iOS 27. Siri mode basically freed the iPhone's Visual Intelligence features from its Camera Control button and brought them into an app people spend a lot more time in. Samsung's Vision feature doesn't sound like it's adding anything new to the concept, but if it makes it even easier to ask AI about the world around you, maybe that will be worth it to some users.

Samsung hasn't announced this feature, and sometimes software appears in betas that never make it to the final release. If Samsung does launch this new Vision feature, it will likely be alongside the Galaxy S27 lineup early next year.

articles.headline: Mercedes set pace in eventful Qatar second practice
keyFacts: World champion Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell during a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix.
The session was interrupted by two red flags, including one for Charles Leclerc's gravel incident and another to recover Pierre Gasly's stranded Alpine.
Drivers will be limited to 27 laps per tyre set, requiring at least two pit stops during Sunday's grand prix due to Pirelli tyre integrity concerns.
body: World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix.
Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session.
Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid.

The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes.
The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin.
Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs.
The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions.
"It was a productive day," said Antonelli. "We tried a lot of things on the car between FP1 and FP2, but in FP2, it seemed like we did a step back with the car.
"But it was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes. It's not easy."

Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them.
He said he feels it will be close between himself and Russell for the race victory, but added: "You can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others."
Norris, meanwhile, said Mercedes "were in a different category" to McLaren, highlighting the Silver Arrows "were quicker in every single corner by miles".
The 2025 world champion added: "We seem in a relatively decent position, similar on pace with Red Bull, and similar-ish to Ferrari. So I'd say it's OK."
Four-time title winner Verstappen said it had been a "difficult day" following his issues with heavy steering towards the end of the session.
"The balance of the car is probably too disconnected at the moment to go fast," he added. "It's costing us quite a bit of lap time."
Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run.
Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed.
The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was sixth on the timesheets, with Leclerc leading Hamilton in seventh and eighth, 1.3 seconds away from Antonelli's time.
The two Racing Bulls of British rookie Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson were ninth and 10th.
Leclerc had to head back into the garage after spinning and going through the gravel when Lawson was just ahead of him at Turn Nine.

The Monegasque driver said the car did not feel right, and the Italian team spent a chunk of time repairing the damage to the floor. After the session he said he lost control after going a little bit early on the throttle.

Ferrari arrived in Qatar after another on-track incident between Leclerc and Hamilton, this time in Las Vegas. The pair made contact and Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, with Hamilton saying on Thursday the team were facing "very, very challenging times".

Leclerc thinks this weekend could potentially be another struggle for the Italian team, who can secure second in the constructors' championship if they can retain at least a 44-point lead over third-placed Red Bull.
"A very, very difficult day. Not even on high fuel were we strong," said Leclerc.
"We are working hard but for some reason, Mercedes is so much faster than I think everyone expected. So the gaps are just a little bit strange."

Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT.

The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included.
Hamilton was told by his engineer in first practice tyre degradation was "much higher than expected" after highlighting his own issues.
Qatar and next week's finale in Abu Dhabi are going ahead as planned despite the ongoing conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran.

articles.headline: Biden book sales lag way behind Obama, Clinton memoirs in first week
keyFacts: Former President Joe Biden's memoir sold 21,000 copies in its first week, falling short of books by Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, Circana reported.
Despite lower sales, the book topped the New York Times Best Sellers list for nonfiction, and publisher Little, Brown and Company expressed pride.
Biden's limited public appearances to promote the book were hampered by his 2025 prostate cancer diagnosis, according to his statements.
body: Former President Joe Biden's new memoir, "Promise Me, America," sold only 21,000 copies in its first week of publication, falling well short of memoirs by former presidents Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, according to market research firm Circana.
In 2020, Obama's "A Promised Land" sold more than 800,000 copies within the first 24 hours of publication, reaching 1 million copies sold by the end of its first week.
Clinton's "My Life" hit the 1 million copies benchmark within two weeks of its release.
BIDEN MEMOIR DRAWS FIRE FOR ‘DENIAL’ AS CRITICS FLAG GAZA, RACIAL-EQUITY OMISSIONS
Despite its apparently low sales numbers, Biden's book still topped the New York Times Best Sellers list for nonfiction.
The book's publisher, Little, Brown and Company, said in a statement it was "immensely proud" of the book reaching the top of the chart.
JOE BIDEN ADDRESSES CRITICS WHO SAID HE HID HIS STAGE 4 CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN UPCOMING MEMOIR
Biden's promotion of the book had been limited by his relatively scant appearances to promote it, an effort hampered by the former president's 2025 prostate cancer diagnosis.

"Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won't be able to do as many conversations about my book as I'd hoped. However, I'm hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves," Biden wrote in a Nov. 8 post on X.
The book's diminished sales numbers compared to Biden's Democratic predecessors appear to follow a trend of the public's relative disinterest in the Bidens' bibliography.
JILL BIDEN SAYS FORMER PRESIDENT WILL LIVE WITH STAGE 4 CANCER 'FOR THE REST OF HIS LIFE,' HAS SLOWED DOWN
Former first lady Jill Biden's June memoir "View from the East Wing," also underperformed compared to the published works of other former first ladies.

Biden's book sold approximately 46,000 copies total, according to Circana. Those numbers are dwarfed by former Sen. Hillary Clinton's "What Happened" and Michelle Obama's "Becoming," each of which surpassed 1 million copies sold.
Former President Joe Biden's post-vice presidential memoir, "Promise Me, Dad," did relatively well compared to the Biden family's other offerings.
The book sold over 300,000 copies, according to Forbes.
Biden appeared at more than 30 public promotion stops while touting that book compared to none for his most recent release.

body: Between Matthew McConaughey, the flesh cathedrals, the space bears, FemJun and the tragedy of Biggs "The Bolt" Keil, the pre-release reveals for Mass Effect-like space RPG Exodus have been a real emotional rollercoaster. It's almost disappointing to learn that the recommended PC system specs are just sort of… fine. Broadly within expectations, by 2026 standards, anyway.

True, you'll need one of those Nvidia RTX 5080 things if you want to play it in 4K at 60fps, but the True Gamer understands that 4K/60FPS is a dangerous and blasphemical overreach, akin to building the Tower of Babel out of cats. 1080p/30FPS was perfectly good enough for Virtua Tennis 3 on Xbox 360, and it'll be perfectly good enough for this game about *squints*… octopus mercenaries. For that, you'll only need an i5-10400, an Nvidia 2060 and a mere 16GB of RAM. Granted, I think new PCs with those components currently cost $200,000, but that isn't Exodus's fault. It's that Jensen Huang who's to blame. Here's the complete spec rundown, anyway.

- GPU: Nvidia RTX 2060 6GB or AMD RX 6600 8GB
- CPU: Intel Core i7-11700 or AMD Ryzen 5 7600
- GPU: Nvidia RTX 3080 10 GB or AMD RX 7700 XT 12GB
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 7 265K or AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- GPU: Nvidia RTX 5080 16GB or AMD RX 9070 XT 16GB

Will you be playing Exodus? I think it looks swankier so far than Owlcat's surprisingly unconvincing The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, that other great hope of people who mourn Mass Effect 5, but I haven't spent any time with a build. It's out 7th April 2027 - I imagine these recommended specs might alter as they stuff in more McConaughey and layer up the space bears.

keyFacts: The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is available on Amazon for $85 during Black Friday, according to CNET.
Amazon stated that the current $85 price is the lowest the Bissell cleaner has been in 365 days.
CNET reports that the Bissell cleaner offers deeper cleaning than the $130 Black Friday priced Shark StainForce, though it requires a cord and more setup.
body: A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite new cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.
Bissell Little Green Mini vs. Shark StainForce
Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner
- Deep-cleans better than the StainForce, pulls dirt and stains up from deep in the carpet
- Completely removed my cats messes with no trace left
- Bigger tanks than the StainForce: 16 ounces clean, 13.5 ounces dirty
- Corded, so no battery to run out mid-clean
- Much more affordable at $130 at full price
- Light and compact at 7 pounds, easy to store
- Corded — 12-foot cord plus 4-foot hose limits your reach and you need an outlet
- More setup than the StainForce: fill the tank, add formula, plug in and clean afterwards
- 16 oz tank is fine for spot jobs but means refills on bigger areas (the full-size Little Green holds 48 oz)

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce.

Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability.
At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.
- Portable and lightweight for use around the house
- Has worked great on multiple soft surfaces, including carpet and upholstery
- Tackles both wet spills and dried-on stains
- The included stain removal spray works better than anything I've used before
- The waste tank needs regular cleaning and airing out to avoid odors

The Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains.

It works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots.

The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life.

The tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that said, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains.
Caddy, dual action spray, stain eliminator tool, crevice tool, reusable spray bottle head, charging cable

I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

The Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference shows in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

The StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

That proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

What I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.
Should you buy the Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner or the Shark StainForce?

If you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a big and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

articles.headline: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
keyFacts: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, according to Counterpoint Research.
Counterpoint Research stated that rising memory costs and constrained supplies driven by AI server demands are putting pressure on handset makers.
Counterpoint forecasts a 6 percent market rebound in 2028 as memory supplies improve and pricing begins to stabilize.
body: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028.

That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers.

The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market.

Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns.

The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing.

As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones.

Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026.

For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases.
"The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang.

"Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets."
Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years.
Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing.

A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery.

"The unusually low 2027 base creates the potential for a robust rebound in 2028 once the memory bottleneck begins to ease. But this should not be interpreted as a return to the old market trajectory," Wang said.
"Some low-end demand has been permanently lost, and the 2028 market will still be about 14 percent below 2025 shipments."
Potential availability of 6G-capable smartphones toward the end of the decade could give the market a boost, but Counterpoint does not expect it to regain its 2025 shipment levels by 2030. ®

articles.headline: Could Donald Trump And Abdul El-Sayed Really Team Up On Universal Healthcare?
keyFacts: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed proposed that President Donald Trump enact Medicare for All under the name TrumpCare.
A White House official rejected the idea, stating that Medicare for All would raise taxes and increase budget deficits.
Democrats preparing to control Congress in January are weighing whether to compromise with Trump or pass bills he might veto.
body: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump’s second-term obsession with his legacy has led him to seek a vast reshaping of Washington, slapping his name on buildings, remaking the White House in his image and even building a literal monument to himself.

Democrats have vociferously fought most of these efforts. But some in the party are still holding out hope they can use Trump’s desire to etch his name into history to convince him to adopt progressive policy, resurrecting a long-held dream Democrats can exploit a latent progressive streak in the president.

These dreams have almost uniformly ended without real results, with whatever ideological flexibility Trump possesses stomped out by hard-liners on his staff and among Republicans in Congress. But some Democrats insist it might be worth trying anyway.

The highest-profile attempt after the midterm elections is coming from Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.), who has used a series of social media posts and interviews to try and impress upon Trump the glory of enacting “Medicare for All,” calling it “TrumpCare” and giving everyone in America a golden TrumpCare card.
“I don’t care whose name’s on it,” El-Sayed said this week. “I just care that people have healthcare.”

“He’s a smart guy,” Trump told the New York Post, only weeks after he headlined a rally where Republicans repeatedly suggested El-Sayed was a terrorist. “He did a good job. He actually did a very good job.”

The president has shared an El-Sayed post about “TrumpCare” on his Truth Social website without comment. But the White House hasn’t signaled any actual openness to the idea, which seems extremely unlikely, considering Trump’s most recent healthcare policies were to cut Medicaid and allow Obamacare subsidies to expire.

Indeed, a White House official panned the idea in an email, pointing to a Council of Economic Advisers analysis that said “Medicare for All” would widen budget deficits by $47 trillion and pay for more than a million gender-affirming surgeries.
“Medicare for All will inevitably increase your taxes,” the official said.
So that’s what they think of that.

Still, El-Sayed’s golden “TrumpCare” cards illustrate a central question confronting Democrats as they prepare to take control of Congress in January: Should they try to cut deals with Trump, or should they pass bills reflecting the popular ideas they campaigned on, even if Trump vetoes everything they send to his desk?
“It’s hard for a president to just spend two years doing nothing but vetoing popular bills.”

The party’s leaders — Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) — have vowed to enact an affordability agenda that, among other things, undoes Trump’s tariffs, reverses his Medicaid cuts, revives Obamacare subsidies and raises the minimum wage, but they haven’t figured out how many individual bills to send or exactly what those bills would look like. One vision calls for lots of little bills that would maximize the political repercussions of a series of unpopular vetoes.

“By moving clear, understandable, important pieces of legislation on a standalone basis, it’s sort of a win-win situation: You either can notch real victories because you get Trump to sign it, or maybe you have to negotiate a little bit and get him to sign a slightly modified version of it, or he vetoes it, and Democrats can say, ‘Look, we passed a major expansion of health insurance, and he vetoed it,’” Bharat Ramamurti, former deputy director of the National Economic Council under President Joe Biden, told HuffPost.

Since 1980, there have been eight instances of one party controlling the House and Senate while the other holds the White House, according to an analysis by Ramamurti. Democratic Congresses have passed significant progressive legislation under Republican presidents, such as a federal minimum wage increase that President George W. Bush signed into law in 2007.

But Ramamurti said Democrats should “play to show” at least as much as they should try to enact merely incremental policy victories. He pointed to a Republican Congress passing welfare reform in the 1990s. President Bill Clinton vetoed two bills before finally signing one into law.

“That can be a template in some ways for getting a president to eventually cave to the political reality, because Congress sets the agenda, and it’s hard for a president to just spend two years doing nothing but vetoing popular bills,” Ramamurti said.
As for Trump: “He’s a very unpredictable guy, and the potential set of outcomes to me seems very broad. And so you might as well try for big-ticket items.”

Since the midterm elections, Trump has threatened to use his veto pen liberally, but he’s also mused occasionally about working with Democrats. He did the same thing in his first term, however, and it never worked out. In 2019, when Democrats controlled the House, he cut a deal with Schumer and then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) for a $2 trillion infrastructure bill, then bailed on the deal a month later because he was mad about Democrats investigating his administration.

Trump has suggested since the election he’d be open to bipartisan immigration reform, acknowledging his deportation policy may have been “too tough,” but it’s another show we’ve seen before. In 2018, Trump invited a bipartisan group of lawmakers to the White House and urged them to write a bill that included a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers. A month later, when the senators unveiled their bill, the White House crapped on it, and it died.
“Trump sent the signal: ‘You guys put a bill on my desk,’” Sen. Tim Kaine (D-Va.), one of the senators involved in the deal, recalled this month in an interview with HuffPost.
“They immediately poured cold water on it,” Kaine said. “Trump did a 180 from what he promised.”

articles.headline: Will we ever see another game like GTA VI?
keyFacts: Rockstar Games reported that Grand Theft Auto VI earned nearly $3.8 billion on its first day of release.
Video game journalist Chris Plante said the title arrives during industry-wide layoffs, rising development budgets, and growing debates over artificial intelligence.
Rockstar will prioritize launching Grand Theft Auto Online and potentially expanding the game before developing a future sequel, Plante stated.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived last week, 13 years after the last installment in the series, to an enormous debut — nearly $3.8 billion in its first day, according to developer Rockstar Games. That’s more than Avengers: Endgame has earned at the global box office across its entire theatrical run, including rereleases.

The game took more than eight years to develop, and Rockstar grew to more than 4,700 employees worldwide during production. In the game, players are catapulted into Leonida, a fictional version of Florida that includes Vice City, the series’ take on Miami.

Unlike past games in the series, you play as a couple, Jason and Lucia, who are trying to make enough money to support their young family and make it out. Maintaining their relationship is just as important as robbing stores or completing missions.

For all that GTA VI is shaping up to be a critically acclaimed triumph, however, it arrives at a difficult moment for the video game industry. Studios have endured years of layoffs and rising development costs, while workers worry about how generative AI could affect their jobs and creative work. Can an industry under this much pressure afford to keep making games this big, or is GTA VI doomed to be the last of its kind?

To find out, Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram spoke with Chris Plante, a video game journalist with about two decades of experience and host of the podcast Post Games . They discussed GTA VI’s long road to release, what could be next for the franchise and whether DLC is on the horizon, and the future of blockbuster gaming more broadly.

Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get podcasts, including Apple Podcasts , Pandora , and Spotify .
Chris, people are saying that this game is the last of its kind. Why are they saying that?

It kind of is, but I think we should be really specific when we say that. The last of its kind means the last of this: thousands and thousands of people trying to make one game without artificial intelligence, and it being a historic, all-consuming moment.

The best shot that we have of another game like this happening is GTA VII. But what I would be wary of is saying there aren’t going to be big-budget video games anymore. If you look at another game that came out just this month, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remake of one of the most famous games ever, one of the most beloved games ever, and it looks stunning. It’s on the Nintendo Switch 2. It is great. And it cost a fraction of what Grand Theft Auto cost [to make]. It took a fraction of the time to create. And yet it still feels absolutely decadent.

You know what a fair comparison would be? We get those Avatar movies — they take forever because they cost a fortune to make, they require all this new technology. That’s your Grand Theft Auto. But you wouldn’t look at an Avatar and say, ‘Well, they’re never going to make expensive movies anymore.’ We still get Dune . We still get Marvel movies. Those things are still happening.

There is a whole separate question about the stability of the highest ends of the industry, the companies that tried to be the Grand Theft Autos: Electronic Arts, the company that makes Madden; companies like Xbox, which owns Activision, which makes Call of Duty.

You might notice I’m saying a lot of which does this but owns that. The consolidation in the industry is real, and it’s a real problem. So there’s going to be turmoil, but it is not the end of video games, and it’s not even the end of big video games.
It sounds like this is a great time for the industry, but it’s actually the opposite.

It’s a great time for people who play video games and a nightmare time for people who make video games. If you play video games right now, you can turn on Steam, which is a storefront on PC, and you can find literally hundreds of games that were released just this week. Over a thousand new games are released every month on Steam. And because of that, it targets not every niche, but close. There is probably something out there for you.

This is a nightmare for people who make games because even Grand Theft Auto, when it comes to PC, is going to live right alongside all those other games. So for the people who do not have the name recognition, who do not have the marketing, you can launch a game that you spent tens, maybe hundreds of millions of dollars on, and it is going to, the same day that it comes out, compete against a brand-new $5 game that was made by three or four people with a whole bunch of contractor support for a very low cost and has just as good of odds, minus the marketing, of being a hit.

Is AI going to make it less risky for big gaming companies to invest in developing something ambitious because maybe they can make it dramatically cheaper and compete with the games that only cost $10 to develop?
AI, as the investment class has it in their head: The answer is no, not whatsoever.
“Looking even beyond games, there’s a lot of reason to be cautious about things that seem like they’re going to make things faster actually, in the long term, making them much slower.”

AI as a tool, it gets more complicated. I think when a lot of people hear AI, they think, I’ve seen a video where I can go on Google and type a prompt, and I say, give me Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, but make it like a Black Eyed Peas concert. And people are like, wow, you seem really out of touch, but I’ll make it for you anyway . And then you have this great game, and you are getting the party started in here. And that is not how any of this works at all.

Games are literally a miracle. My former colleague, Frank Lantz, who’s an educator and game designer, would compare it to art, if you also had to build a skyscraper or a highway. You have to both make the architecture and make the art. It’s unhinged. We do not have this world where games just are going to materialize.

Now where it gets really complicated and it gets really messy inside the industry is using AI tools for things like coding. And this is very controversial amongst a certain corner of video games culture and video game developers. There are people who want a full ban, that we are not using AI on anything, that we need to protect jobs, and that it shouldn’t be used for generating images or art or music or code.

And then there are people who say, but I use AI for code. I think it is relatively common, and that is somewhat of a controversial take, but it is what I hear from so many people I talk to who are on that side of game development, to be using it when you are programming as a tool.

I think there’s a lot of promises, but I think that, again, looking even beyond games, there’s a lot of reason to be cautious about things that seem like they’re going to make things faster actually, in the long term, making them much slower.
And we still live in a world where it makes sense to start developing a GTA VII?
It does for Rockstar for sure, though I don’t think that they will be in a rush to do it anytime soon, for a few reasons.

One, they still need to get Grand Theft Auto Online out. That’s where the real money is. Grand Theft Auto Online drops people into the city of each new game. Grand Theft Auto V did it with LA. Now you’re going to have it in Miami. And that is where people can get lost for years and years and years, and they can start charging you for little incremental things like cool new outfits or fancy cars or spots to live. So that’s going to be their priority.

There has been word or rumor that they might just expand Grand Theft Auto VI, that we would see more cities. Who knows if that’s true? It would be a different approach, but the game began as a thing called Project Americas and was supposed to be a much larger game. So that could be one way that it grows rather than a GTA VII: We just see a GTA VI that gets bigger and bigger, not unlike Fortnite, but we’re going to get more of it.
Do you want to put in an early guess as to what year GTA VII comes out so that someone listening to this in, I don’t know, 10, 15, 20 years can be like, wow, that guy nailed it ?

Damn. Actually, I was going to say that I think it would be sooner than 13 years, and I’m not sure I actually believe that. I’m going to put it at, let’s say, 2037. I’ll see you in 11 years. Does that sound good?
If all goes well for our industries, yes.
Yeah. Better odds in the Grand Theft Auto business. I mean, hey, we can always turn into a romantic duo performing a life of crime.

articles.headline: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
keyFacts: French authorities ordered actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting actress Charlotte Arnould.
The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, particularly in the arts.
Depardieu denies the rape allegations, and his lawyer said he disputes the ruling without specifying if he will appeal.
body: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault

PARIS — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.
Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.

Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.

Depardieu, 77, has denied the rape allegations. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told The Associated Press that he disputes Thursday's ruling, without specifying whether he would challenge it before France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.
The ruling upholds part of an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send Depardieu to trial.
The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.
A French cinema icon faces a #MeToo reckoning
With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, Depardieu dominated French cinema for half a century.
He became one of the country's most recognizable cultural exports, earning an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."
But accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.

On Nov. 16, Depardieu abandoned his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021, accepting an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issuing a public apology that marked a departure from his earlier denials in that case.
"I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered," he said in a written statement.
Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 of groping a set decorator and an assistant during the filming of "Les Volets Verts" ("The Green Shutters").
The court also ordered his name to be listed in France's national sex offender database.

"On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did," Depardieu said.
Accusations against Depardieu sparked a national debate
The controversy surrounding Depardieu intensified in December 2023 after a television documentary showed him repeatedly making obscene remarks and gestures during a 2018 trip to North Korea.

Even French President Emmanuel Macron weighed in, drawing criticism from women's rights activists when he said the actor "makes France proud." Macron invoked the presumption of innocence and said he would not participate in a "manhunt."
The controversy exposed divisions in a country where some prominent cultural figures had pushed back against the #MeToo movement.
In 2018, actress Catherine Deneuve and 99 other women signed an open letter defending men's freedom to make advances toward women and warning against what they saw as the movement's excesses.

Born in 1948 into a working-class family in the central French city of Châteauroux, Depardieu overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors. His career spanned hundreds of films, from "The Last Metro" and "Jean de Florette" to the popular "Asterix" franchise.
His excesses off-screen also made international headlines, notably when he accepted a Russian passport from Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.

articles.headline: Donald Trump’s ‘Despicable’ Iran War Remark To U.S. Service Member Sparks Backlash
keyFacts: Donald Trump told a U.S. service member during a Thanksgiving call that the timing of the end of the war with Iran is up to him.
Trump stated that negotiations are ongoing to give Iran a chance to make a deal, though he questioned their sanity.
Critics on social media condemned the remarks as despicable and inappropriate for service members deployed during the holiday.
body: Donald Trump drew backlash on Thursday over a comment about when his war with Iran will end, which he made during a Thanksgiving call with U.S. service members.

Speaking from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida to a service member stationed in the Middle East, Trump said he and first lady Melania Trump “join millions this holiday to pray for your safety and success.”
“You’re going to continue that deployment and we have victory at hand,” he continued.
As for when that victory might come in the conflict he launched nine months ago, Trump said: “It’s going to be — whenever, sort of, whenever I want it to be.”
“To be honest, we’re trying to be nice, we’re trying to let them, we’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives,” he added of ongoing negotiations with Iran.
“But I’m not sure if they are going to take advantage of that. Some people question why, are they crazy? Maybe they are,” he said.
Critics seized on Trump’s suggestion that the timing of the war’s conclusion was effectively his to decide, with one describing his remarks as “despicable.”
Trump, after launching the war in February, initially said it would last a matter of weeks. It continues.
“Just the message service members want to hear on Thanksgiving while away from their families fighting his war of choice,” one wrote on X.

articles.headline: Why is there a shortage of 'wizard' elevator mechanics?
keyFacts: A shortage of elevator mechanics is worsening in the US and UK despite average US salaries of $110,000, industry figures say.
The labor shortage delays elevator repairs, stranding residents such as the elderly and wheelchair users who rely on lifts.
Industry experts suggest teaching trade basics in high schools and offering tax breaks to help attract new mechanics.
body: Some of them are angry. Nerves are frayed. Many of them are just relieved that he's here.

When a lift stops working in Chicago, frazzled building managers might get a visit from Jim Lembesis. For more than 47 years, Lembesis has repaired and upgraded lifts. He says he understands why staff and residents are so anxious to have things working again.
"They wait and they wait," says Lembesis, a field technician for Parkway Elevators. "There's a lot of frustration. Sometimes it's a repeat issue. It's a never-ending cycle, you know what I mean?"

The widely reported shortage of lift and escalator mechanics in the US, which is also a problem in many other countries, has got worse over time, he adds: "It's been like night and day compared to when I started."
Everyone needs a lift now and again. Some people depend on them â elderly residents of high-rise buildings, say, or wheelchair users.

Storm-damaged lifts in Hawaiian apartment blocks this year left some residents trapped, external in their homes for weeks. A lack of mechanics, and problems sourcing parts, were blamed for the repair delays.
In the US, the average salary for a lift mechanic, external is $110,000 (Â£83,000). And yet people in the industry say it is difficult to attract new workers.

Sure, says Lembesis, you do encounter some dangers in a job like this. There are risks of falling from a great height â or being electrocuted. Once, he was even hit on the head with an umbrella by an elderly lady after he rescued her from a stuck lift.

But there are so many skills to learn, and great camaraderie and knowledge-sharing among mechanics, he says. As one recruiter puts it, these technicians amaze people with their ability to fix things. They are like "wizards". The overall-clad shamans who know how to get modern life running again.

Nine times out of 10, the problem is with the doors, says Lembesis. These components repeatedly move back and forth. "People hit them with carts, and dirt and debris [falls into them]," says Lembesis. "[The doors] take the most beating."
Mechanics often keep various spare door parts in their vehicles, ready to use.

But technicians like Lembesis don't just have to get lifts working, they also have to verify the lifts are safe. He remembers one case, decades ago, getting called out to a burning building. His role was to ensure the lifts, which were being drenched with huge volumes of water, were still safe to use while firefighters tackled the blaze.
"I was there for 15 hours that night," he says. "Everyone, on the way out of the door, shook my hand."

Finding good lift technicians is "becoming more difficult" says Matt Hollinshead, president of the US National Association for Elevator Contractors. "We have a four-year apprenticeship," he says. That's the first hurdle. And many states require certification or licensing before you can work on lifts.
"We have a vast array of equipment that has to be maintained in the United States." Some lifts are 100-years-old. As time goes on, the technological knowledge required to repair them only grows.

Hollinshead says that weeks or months-long delays to lift repairs are not typically due to staff shortages but that, in such cases, it's likely that a particular part isn't readily available. Manufacturing a replacement hydraulic cylinder takes six to 12 weeks, he notes.
But the lack of technicians does mean that that building managers might have to wait days before someone can even diagnose what's wrong with a lift after it stops working.
Hollinshead says teaching the basics of the trade in high schools or technical schools could entice more people into the role.

Matt Allred, a recruiter and host of The Elevator Careers Podcast, emphasises the many skills that lift mechanics require. "You're a little bit of a wizard, right? You show up and if you can fix it â 'Wow!'."
He blames major lift companies, in part, for locking down maintenance contracts, making it difficult or impossible for third-party repairers to intervene when a lift fails.

Two large lift manufacturers approached by BBC News declined interviews. The chief executive of Otis, one of the firms, said in May that her company was struggling to hire enough staff, external to meet demand. The firm also states on its website, external that the shortage of lift mechanics affects "almost every part of the world".
However, a spokesman for Otis claimed its "US talent pipeline" was healthy, and declined an interview.

Everyone else who spoke to BBC News said hiring was challenging in the US. Allred was recently contacted by a major lift company and asked to help them find a technician. "I was surprised that a major company would reach out to a little recruiting shop," he says, suggesting that this reflects the extent of the labour shortage.

That shortage is also a problem in the UK. "It is bad and getting worse," says Dave Cooper, president of the Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers, who is also chief executive of a lift and escalator engineering consultancy.
"We've known food delivery companies to refuse to deliver to flats above the ground floor because the lift is out of service."
Offering better tax breaks to companies that train lift mechanics could help ensure that plenty of workers continue to enter the industry, he adds.

Training to be a lift mechanic is "not a quick route to competency â and it requires people to stick at it for the long term" says Karen Slade, head of assessment at the Lift and Escalator Industry Association (Leia).
Continued investment in training and attracting new workers is "essential", according to Leia. There are currently 259 active lift and escalator apprentices in the UK, the body adds.
Back in Chicago, Lembesis is working with two younger mechanics who have been "really good", he says, so there's at least some hope for the future.
He stresses again how rewarding he finds his work. The people for whom he fixes lifts tend to be very appreciative.
"I love that. You get that reaction from the customers," he says. "Without them, you got nothing."

articles.headline: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
keyFacts: Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, according to a Journal report.
Nvidia is assessing whether regional partners meet U.S. export requirements after Chinese companies accessed chips remotely.
The Institute for Progress estimated that remote data centers supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.
body: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.
